actions.plan: Repository has no resolvable HEAD; list refs to select a starting commit, then search for the leads endpoint source.
Inspect the three refs to identify their nature (patch vs vulnerable revision) via messages and parents.
Search for leads route/controller in the release commit to locate the entry point and handler.
Read constants to find route registration variable, then find router/handler.
Read the leads router to find the handler and the mass-assignment defect.
Read the leads controller to identify the mass-assignment operation in createLeadInChatflow.
Read leads service to find where req.body is persisted (mass assignment sink).
Read Lead entity to confirm assignable fields for mass assignment.

actions.summary: Inspected ref 55b6913c (release 3.0.12) contains a POST /api/v1/leads handler that forwards the raw req.body to leadsService.createLead, where Object.assign(newLead, body) plus repository.save() produces the mass-assignment behavior named in the advisory. Route path, whitelist entry, router, controller, service and Lead entity were all read at that commit. Limitations: no fix commit and no vulnerable_commit were supplied, so the chosen SHA is a locally inspected revision carrying the defect rather than an advisory-confirmed affected version; deployment conditions, affected version ranges, and authentication/whitelist implications come only from the advisory title/identifiers and were not independently confirmed. Suggested coarse category (Input Validation) is inferred, not advisory-sourced.

critical_operation.desc: Unfiltered request body is merged onto the Lead entity (attacker-controllable attributes such as chatflowid/chatId/name/email/phone), then persisted via repository.create/save on lines 31-32.

entry_point.desc: Externally reachable POST handler declared for /api/v1/leads; it only checks that req.body exists and forwards the whole client body unvalidated to the leads service.
